newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Dacom sees '96 net rising to 20 bln won.
newsitem.headline: Dacom sees '96 net rising to 20 bln won.

text.p: Dacom Corp, South Korea's second long-distance telephone service provider, expects to see its net profit rising to 20 billion won on sales of 650 billion won in calendar 1996, a senior company official said on Thursday.
Dacom posted a net profit of 13.5 billion won in 1995 on a revenue of 370 billion won.
"The growth will come primarily from the addition of our domestic long-distance service," said Cho Yong-wan, Dacom's director of finance. Dacom launched its domestic long-distance service in January.
Dacom forecast that its net income would reach 150 billion won with sales climbing to 2 trillion won in the year 2000.
The telecommunications company plans to invest 2.5 trillion won in the business between 1996 and 2000.

Cho, speaking before investors and analysts at a UBS Securities Investor Forum, said he did not anticipate that the launch of a third international long-distance service due next year would hurt Dacom's business.
"We think the competitor will take up only five percent of the market share next year. We believe that will come out of Korea Telecom's share rather than ours," he said.

Dacom has targeted a market share of 16 percent this year and sees this growing to 20 percent by the year 2000. State-backed Korea Telecom is seen holding 60 percent and the new provider 10 percent of the market share, Cho said.
